sentences.text: Spitrasaurus was an extinct genus of cryptoclidid plesiosaur, a member of the family Cryptoclididae.
The type species of this genus is Spitrasaurus wensaasi.
The holotype of the related species S. larseni is a poorly preserved juvenile skeleton that includes cranial remains.
The genus name Spitrasaurus is an abbreviation for Spitsbergen Travel.
The species names wensaasi and larseni honor volunteers Tommy Wensås and Stig Larsen, respectively.
The holotype of Spitrasaurus larseni was found in 2010 and is a juvenile skeleton containing cervical vertebrae and skull material.
Fossils of Spitrasaurus were found between 2004 and 2010 in Spitsbergen within the Agardhfjellet Formation.
A cervical vertebra found in the Kimmeridge Clay Formation in England was tentatively assigned to Spitrasaurus in 2014.
Spitrasaurus lived during the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic, between 149.2 and 143.1 million years ago.
Spitrasaurus is known from the uppermost Jurassic of central Spitsbergen, Norway, and likely also from Kimmeridge, England.
